source.title_on_document: The Ideation–Execution Gap: Execution Outcomes of LLM-Generated versus Human Research Ideas

supplement.where: Appendices A onward in the same PDF; data at https://github.com/NoviScl/AI-Researcher (p. 1, footnote 1); preregistration at https://osf.io/ckxtp (p. 3, footnote 2)
supplement.holds: Review form (App. A), institutions of participants (App. B, Tables 7-8), score distributions (App. C), ideation-execution correlations (App. D, Table 9), robustness excluding 6 AI ideas (App. F, Table 10), metric correlations (Tables 11-12), example executed papers

paper_design_summary: 43 analyzed expert NLP researchers each executed one randomly assigned research idea, supplied either by a Claude-3.5-Sonnet ideation agent or by a human expert, using ideas from Si et al. (2025) (PDF pp. 2-4, Sections 2.1-2.2). Participants averaged 103 hours overall, with means of 112.6 hours in the human-idea arm and 93.7 hours in the AI-idea arm; they had a three-month execution window and submitted a codebase and a paper of at least 4 pages (PDF p. 3, Introduction; p. 4, Section 2.2; p. 5, Table 2). 58 blinded expert reviewers scored novelty, excitement, effectiveness, soundness, and overall quality, and the authors compared execution scores with the reused pre-execution ideation ratings (PDF p. 3, Section 2.1; pp. 6-7, Tables 3-5).

studies.label: Execution study (LLM vs human research ideas)

assignment.what_was_assigned: Source of the research idea to execute: an LLM-generated idea or a human-expert-written idea, drawn from the participant's preferred topics
assignment.quote: we first ask for their preferred topics among our 7 candidate topics, and then we randomly assign either an LLM-generated idea or a human-written idea to them from their selected topics.
assignment.locator: p. 4, Section 2.2 (Random Idea Assignment); also p. 3, Section 2.1
assignment.prereg_locator: PDF p. 3, Section 2.1 and footnote 2: https://osf.io/ckxtp; preregistration is stated in the paper; the registration itself was not read.

arms.name: AI idea
arms.description: Executes an anonymized research idea generated by an LLM agent based on Claude-3.5-Sonnet

arms.name: Human idea
arms.description: Executes an anonymized research idea written by a human expert

participants.exclusions: 66 participants were onboarded and 43 completed. One project was terminated because the assigned idea was too vague and infeasible; the other noncompletions were attributed to personal reasons (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1; p. 4, Section 2.2). The full pre-attrition randomized total and its arm allocation are not unambiguously reported, so n_randomized remains null.
participants.who: Expert NLP researchers recruited via social media, direct outreach, and conferences, screened by profile and interview; mean 15.3 (human arm) and 14.3 (AI arm) papers on Google Scholar; from 7 countries
participants.country: US, Australia, India, UK, Nepal, Singapore, Canada
participants.quote: After basic profile screening, we onboarded a total of 66 participants for the execution task, among whom 43 completed the task in the end.
participants.locator: PDF p. 5, Sections 3.1-3.2 and Table 2; analyzed arm sizes also in p. 3, Table 1 and p. 7, Table 4.

ai_tool.name_model: LLM ideation agent based on Claude-3.5-Sonnet (ideas from Si et al. 2025)
ai_tool.how_used: The supplied AI idea was the input for producing the assigned research project (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 2.1-2.2). AI availability is coded yes for this supplied-ideas intervention; the paper does not describe randomized chatbot access during execution. The scored output is the assigned project at completion, with no separate assessment of unassisted work after AI removal.

task.description: Execute an assigned NLP research idea into a full project: implement and run the proposed experiments, submit a codebase, and write a short paper of at least 4 pages in ACL format
task.duration: Three-month window; mean 112.6 hours (human arm) and 93.7 hours (AI arm), Table 2, p. 5

outcomes.name: Overall paper-quality/conference-acceptability score of executed project (1-10)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Blinded expert rating of overall paper quality/conference acceptability on a 1-10 scale, calibrated to an ACL short paper: 1 is critically flawed, trivial, or wrong; 6 is marginally above the acceptance threshold; 10 denotes a seminal paper. This is coded usefulness (quality), while novelty is rated separately (PDF p. 21, Appendix A, item 19; p. 18, item 10). Tables 4-5 use project-level average reviewer scores for 43 outputs, one per analyzed participant (19 human-idea projects; 24 AI-idea projects); Table 5 compares execution-minus-ideation score changes. The separate Table 3 comparison uses unit=rating, n_units=181 (85 human-condition reviews; 96 AI-condition reviews), written by 58 reviewers with 4-5 reviews per project; its SDs and tests treat reviews as independent and are not project-level statistics (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1; p. 6, Table 3 and Section 4.1; p. 7, Tables 4-5). Appendix F, Table 10 (PDF p. 29), is a sensitivity analysis excluding 6 AI ideas whose proposed human evaluation was removed, not a separate study or outcome. Timing is the completion of the assigned project within its three-month window, with the supplied idea used during production (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 2.1-2.2).

contrasts.reported: Project-level execution scores (unit=output, N=43; Human n=19, AI n=24), using each project's average reviewer score: Human mean 3.968 vs AI mean 3.406; two-sided two-sample t-test, FDR-adjusted p=0.175. Project-level SDs and SEs are not reported in this table.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 7, Table 4 (execution-score block and caption); p. 6, Section 4.1.

contrasts.reported: Project-level execution-minus-ideation score gap for the same projects (Human n=19, AI n=24): Human -0.628 vs AI -1.976; printed difference (Human minus AI) 1.348; FDR-adjusted p=0.004**. These are raw rating-scale changes; negative gaps denote score decreases. Values are transcribed as printed in Table 5, without recomputation.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 7, Table 5 and Section 4.2; project counts in Table 4.

contrasts.reported: Review-level execution scores (unit=rating, n_units=181): Human mean 4.00 (SD 1.59, n=85 reviews) vs AI mean 3.41 (SD 1.46, n=96 reviews); one-sided two-sample t-test, FDR-adjusted p=0.01*. Table 3 treats reviews as independent observations; these are review-level, not project-level, SDs and p-values.
contrasts.locator: PDF p. 6, Table 3 and caption; reviewer counts in p. 5, Section 3.1.

outcomes.name: Technical soundness score of executed project (1-10)
outcomes.question: with_ai
outcomes.measure_detail: Blinded expert rating of technical correctness, methodological rigor, experiment design, and appropriate datasets, metrics, and baselines on a 1-10 scale (PDF pp. 19-20, Appendix A, item 14). The numerical arm comparison is review-level: Table 3 treats 181 ratings (85 human-condition reviews; 96 AI-condition reviews) as independent observations. 58 reviewers provided 4-5 reviews per project across 43 projects (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1; p. 6, Table 3 and Section 4.1). Tables 4-5 do not report project-level soundness means or an ideation-execution soundness gap (PDF p. 7). The output is the assigned project at completion within the three-month execution window (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 2.1-2.2).

contrasts.reported: Review-level execution scores (unit=rating, n_units=181): Human mean 5.38 (SD 1.72, n=85 reviews) vs AI mean 4.73 (SD 1.82, n=96 reviews); one-sided two-sample t-test, FDR-adjusted p=0.01*. Table 3 treats reviews as independent observations.

sample_overlap.shares_participants_with: Execution-participant overlap is not stated. The assigned human/AI idea corpus and pre-execution ideation ratings are reused from Si, Yang, and Hashimoto (2025), Can LLMs Generate Novel Research Ideas? A Large-Scale Human Study with 100+ NLP Researchers (arXiv:2409.04109). This is shared-corpus/rating provenance, not an additional independent ideation sample or a confirmed count of shared execution participants.
sample_overlap.quote: The LLM and human ideas used in our execution study are taken from our previous ideation study,
sample_overlap.locator: PDF p. 3, Section 2.1; p. 12, Section 7.2 (Idea Scope); p. 16, reference to Si et al. (2025).

company_involvement.description: The acknowledgement lists a gift from Amazon among the project's financial support. It does not establish company involvement in study design or analysis.

eligibility.reason: The paper individually randomizes researchers to execute supplied AI-generated or human-written ideas, satisfying the supplied-ideas intervention criterion (PDF pp. 3-4, Sections 2.1-2.2). Only 43 people were analyzed, 19 in the human-idea arm and 24 in the AI-idea arm, below the required 50 analyzed people (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1 and Table 2; p. 7, Table 4). 66 is the onboarded count, not a clearly reported pre-attrition randomized total; reviewer and review counts do not count toward the participant threshold (PDF p. 5, Section 3.1). Expert ratings of the executed projects include novelty and output quality, satisfying the scored-output criterion (PDF p. 6, Table 3; pp. 18-21, Appendix A). The field_rct classification reflects the assigned real research projects completed over a three-month window (PDF pp. 3-5, Sections 2.1-3.1). This remains a small randomized experiment for the screening report, with context_class=none.

one_line_finding: Projects executed from LLM ideas lost more review score from ideation to execution than projects from human ideas (Δ Human–AI gap: overall 1.348, p FDR 0.004; novelty 1.039, p FDR 0.025; Table 5, p. 7), while idea-level execution scores did not differ significantly (overall Human 3.968 vs AI 3.406, p FDR 0.175; Table 4, p. 7).
notes: The full markdown was read through its end, including Appendices A-H and all embedded example papers; the PDF on file has 131 pages. Recorded numerical results and correction evidence were checked against the corresponding PDF pages. Pre-execution ratings and ideas come from Si et al. (2025), so the ideation-execution gaps reuse that corpus and its ratings; execution-participant overlap is not reported (PDF p. 3, Section 2.1; p. 12, Section 7.2). Project-level execution comparisons, project-level execution-minus-ideation gap comparisons, and review-level comparisons are separate contrasts within each outcome, not independent studies. The gaps are raw score changes, and their printed positive differences are Human minus AI; Table 5 entries are preserved as printed without deriving or reconciling them from rounded means (PDF p. 7, Tables 4-5). The recorded outcomes are the main evaluation metrics; faithfulness to the assigned outline and codebase quality are designated execution-control metrics by the paper (PDF p. 4, Section 2.2; p. 6, Table 3). The main paper labels https://github.com/NoviScl/AI-Researcher as a data release (PDF p. 1, footnote 1); a separate study-code release was not verified. The preregistration statement was confirmed in the PDF, but the registration itself was not read.
